name: Curved-space Maxwell equations, Gauss' law sqrt(-g) F^{tr} = Q, and the Maxwell stress-energy T_ab = (F_ac F_b^c - g_ab F^2/4)/(4 pi); 'spherical symmetry admits only F_{tr}'

source.located: Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019 (Dec 1997), eqs (4.24)-(4.27) [curved-space Maxwell], (7.107) [T_{mu nu}, 1/4pi], (7.108) [most general spherically symmetric F: F_tr = f(r,t), F_{theta phi} = g(r,t) sin theta], (7.111)-(7.112) [RN with electric q and magnetic p]. Restated for the DYNAMICAL case by Dafermos arXiv:gr-qc/0307013 Prop. 2.1 eq (22) F = (e/r^2) Omega^2 du^dv, eq (25) T = e^2/(2 r^4) gbar + (e^2/r^2) gamma [units G_ab = 2 T_ab, no 1/4pi], and by Maedler-Gannouji-Gallo arXiv:2503.24162 eqs (2.7),(2.13),(3.5b),(5.7b) [Q constant, Q_lambda = 0 for pure Einstein-Maxwell] and (5.11) [Misner-Sharp M with Q0^2 (1/r_B - 1/r)]. The underlying classical results (Maxwell 1865; Reissner 1916 / Nordstrom 1918; the RN-with-monopole solution) are pre-arXiv and NAMED-NOT-READ; what was read is Carroll's exact restatement.

published_statement: Carroll (7.107): T_{mu nu} = (1/4pi)(F_{mu rho} F_nu^rho - (1/4) g_{mu nu} F_{rho sigma} F^{rho sigma}). Carroll (7.108): 'Since we have spherical symmetry, the most general field strength tensor will have components F_tr = f(r,t) = -F_rt, F_{theta phi} = g(r,t) sin theta = -F_{phi theta}, where f(r,t) and g(r,t) are some functions to be determined by the field equations, and components not written are zero. F_tr corresponds to a radial electric field, while F_{theta phi} corresponds to a radial magnetic field.' Field equations (7.109): g^{mu nu} nabla_mu F_{nu sigma} = 0, nabla_[mu F_{nu rho]} = 0. Solution (7.111)-(7.112): Delta = 1 - 2GM/r + G(p^2+q^2)/r^2, F_tr = -q/r^2, F_{theta phi} = p sin theta; 'Conservatives are welcome to set p = 0 if they like.' Curved-space Maxwell (4.24)-(4.27): nabla_mu F^{nu mu} = 4 pi J^nu, nabla_[mu F_{nu lambda]} = 0, equivalently d(*F) = 4 pi (*J), dF = 0; Carroll (3.28): nabla_mu V^mu = (1/sqrt|g|) d_mu(sqrt|g| V^mu), which is what turns the source-free inhomogeneous equation into d_a(sqrt(-g) F^{ab}) = 0. Dafermos Prop 2.1 (22),(25): in ANY spherically symmetric Einstein-Maxwell(-scalar) spacetime the Maxwell field is F = (e/r^2) Omega^2 du^dv with e a CONSTANT and its stress-energy is e^2/(2r^4) gbar + (e^2/r^2) gamma, i.e. rho = -p_r = p_T = e^2/(2 r^4) in units with G_ab = 2 T_ab.
published_hypotheses: H1 spherical symmetry: SO(3) acts by isometry preserving F (Dafermos sec. 2 states this explicitly; Carroll 'we have spherical symmetry')

H2 Maxwell's equations in curved spacetime in the minimally coupled, torsion-free form (Carroll 4.24-4.27; Carroll p.108 names the alternative nabla_mu[(1+alpha R)F^{nu mu}] and sets alpha = 0 by the equivalence principle -- that IS a hypothesis, not a theorem)
H3 source-free region: J = 0 (electrovac) for the Gauss-law integration; charges only inside the region

H4 the metric ansatz -e^{2alpha(r,t)} dt^2 + e^{2beta(r,t)} dr^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 (Carroll 7.106), i.e. areal radius used as coordinate (Carroll) or the general warped product with R(t,r) (Dafermos, Maedler et al.)
H5 both an electric charge q and a magnetic charge p are admitted; setting p = 0 is a CHOICE (Carroll 7.112 'Conservatives are welcome to set p = 0')

H6 Gaussian units, signature -+++, with T_{mu nu} carrying 1/4pi (Carroll 7.107); Dafermos and Maedler et al. use G_ab = 2T_ab / kappa = 8 pi with no 1/4pi, so the same field gives rho = e^2/(2 r^4) there -- the numerical prefactor is a unit convention
H7 linear Maxwell theory (the Lagrangian -F^2/16pi, Maedler eq 2.1); nonlinear electrodynamics is outside

rederivation.outcome: 33/33 checks pass (sympy 1.14.0, python 3.11). A: solving L_xi F = 0 for the three SO(3) Killing fields on a general 2-form gives F = E(t,r) dt^dr + B(t,r) sin(theta) dtheta^dphi and nothing else (a t-theta component violates invariance; f(theta) must be sin theta). B: d_a(sqrt(-g)F^{ab}) = 0 is exactly d_t u = d_r u = 0 with u = E R^2 e^{-Phi-Lambda}, so E = Q e^{Phi+Lambda}/R^2 is UNIQUE; dF = 0 forces B = P constant. C: sqrt(-g) F^{tr} = -Q sin(theta), not +Q (comment misprint); R^2 e^{-Phi-Lambda} F_tr = Q holds. D: rho = (Q^2+P^2)/(8 pi R^4), j = 0, p_r = -rho, p_T = +rho (both angular), all off-diagonal T_ab = 0, F^2 = 2(B_phys^2 - E_phys^2), rho = (E_phys^2+B_phys^2)/8pi in the orthonormal frame. E: rho + p_r = 0, rho + p_T = 2 rho > 0, traceless, rho > 0, DEC saturated. F: Misner-Sharp MS-r and MS-t residuals vanish identically for ARBITRARY Phi(t,r), Lambda(t,r), R(t,r) with m = M - (Q^2+P^2)/(2R); 1 - 2m/R is the dyonic RN function; m < 0 iff R < (Q^2+P^2)/(2M). G: Heaviside-Lorentz rho = (Q^2+P^2)/(2R^4) = 4 pi x Gaussian (matches Dafermos e^2/(2 r^4)); SI form and section 4's X/a integral agree. H: the owner's own electrovac() and birkhoff_residuals(), imported by path and not edited, reproduce their asserted results and agree with the independent P = 0 specialisation.

later_literature.what: States the general spherically symmetric F has BOTH F_tr and F_{theta phi} = g sin theta; the tree's 'admits only F_tr' is the p = 0 sub-case. Everything else in the tree's use is confirmed verbatim (T with 1/4pi, RN mass function).

In every spherically symmetric Einstein-Maxwell(-scalar) solution F = (e/r^2) Omega^2 du^dv with e constant, T = e^2/(2r^4) gbar + (e^2/r^2) gamma: rho = -p_r = p_T in the fully dynamical (double-null) setting, and the renormalised Hawking mass is m + e^2/(2r) -- the same m = M - Q^2/(2R) structure the tree's Birkhoff step uses. Dafermos too takes only the electric component (no F_{theta phi}), as a modelling choice.

Affine-null formulation: Q is the charge function (2.7), the Maxwell equation gives Q_lambda = 0 with no scalar field (3.5b, 5.6b), the Misner-Sharp mass carries Q0^2(1/r_B - 1/r) (5.11), and the general vacuum-plus-charge solution is RN (5.8). The Maxwell field is written with the single component F_{w lambda} (gauge A = alpha dw) -- again the P = 0 choice, made implicitly.

Necessary and sufficient conditions for a spherically symmetric spacetime to be static in terms of stress-energy eigenvalues in the Birkhoff frame: if mu_1 (radial pressure eigenvalue) depends on r alone then the spacetime is static with h = 1 - 2m(r)/r and a generalised TOV relation (28). Electrovac has mu_1 = -rho = -(Q^2+P^2)/(8 pi r^4), a function of r alone, so the tree's 'mass function is frozen' Birkhoff step is an instance of a general theorem rather than an isolated computation. Weiner assumes T diagonal in the Birkhoff frame (kappa = 0); electrovac satisfies it (j = 0, check D2/D6).

lacked_data: This is a theorem, not a measurement, so the only 'data' a 1916-1997 author could have lacked is whether magnetic monopoles exist (Carroll 1997: 'never been observed'), and that datum was and is unknown. The re-derivation shows the conclusion is INSENSITIVE to it: with P != 0 every quantity the tree rests on (rho > 0 at every R, p_r = -rho, j = 0, the frozen Misner-Sharp mass m = M - (Q^2+P^2)/2R, m < 0 iff R < (Q^2+P^2)/2M) holds with Q^2 -> Q^2 + P^2 (checks D1-F4). The two numerical constants the owner file carries (eps0, G) belong to a different section, and CODATA 2022 leaves G identical and moves eps0 by 6.8e-10 relative, which cancels in the ratio r_c/a. Evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result: no datum, known or unknown, moves the conclusion. Evidence for it, in a narrow sense: the tree's own author lacked (or omitted) the magnetic sector Carroll writes down, and the words 'admits only F_tr' are inaccurate as a statement about spherical symmetry -- an omission in the statement, with no consequence for the conclusion.
grade_evidence: The tree's STATEMENT 'spherical symmetry admits only F_{tr}' / 'the ONLY spherically symmetric field' (drivensource.py:286, 302) holds on a smaller class than it claims: the source (Carroll 7.108, READ) and the machine check (A1-A4, Lie derivative under all three rotation Killing fields) both give F_tr AND F_{theta phi} = P sin theta. The hypothesis 'P = 0' is in force in the tree and unnamed. This is exactly the NARROWED clause 'a hypothesis the tree drops'. It is NOT WRONG: no downstream conclusion fails -- every rests_on item (rho > 0 everywhere, NEC saturation, the frozen mass function, ledger D4's counterexample) survives the widening with Q^2 -> Q^2 + P^2, re-derived here (D1-F4, 33/33). Two further discrepancies are recorded and neither is a refutation: the comment 'sqrt(-g) F^{tr} = Q' is off by a sign and a sin(theta) (C1; the coded field is right), and only the divergence half of Maxwell is checked (dF = 0 holds, B2). Units are internally consistent across the file's two systems (G1-G2). No datum moves the conclusion (CODATA 2022 READ).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner naming 'no magnetic charge (P = 0)' as a hypothesis at lines 286/302, or restating the result for the dyonic field (Q^2 -> Q^2 + P^2), plus correcting the Gauss-law comment to R^2 e^{-Phi-Lambda} F_tr = Q; both are one-line edits to a file this workflow does not touch. To WRONG: a spherically symmetric Maxwell field (in linear, minimally coupled Maxwell theory) with rho + p_r != 0 or rho <= 0 somewhere, or a Misner-Sharp residual that fails for some Phi, Lambda, R -- the sympy checks quantify over arbitrary functions, so this would require an error in the check itself.
